--- title: "Suppression is a status" jupyter: coi-docs --- Surveillance sources hide small or unreliable numbers for good reasons — protecting privacy in a small population, avoiding an estimate too noisy to publish. But "hidden" is not the same fact as "missing," and a lot of downstream harm comes from collapsing the two into one blank cell. `value_status` is a closed, documented enum on every row of `measure.observation`: | `value_status` | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `reported` | value published | | `suppressed_small_count` | below the source's count threshold | | `suppressed_complementary` | suppressed to prevent back-calculation | | `suppressed_reliability` | suppressed because the estimate is unreliable | | `not_available` | source publishes no value for this unit | | `not_applicable` | combination is meaningless (e.g. cervix × male) | The invariant: **`value` is `NULL` whenever `value_status` is not `'reported'`, and never otherwise.** No reader has to parse a sentinel (`"*"`, `"3 or fewer"`, `-1`) to find out — and no reader can accidentally average a suppressed cell in as a zero, because there's no number there to average. ## Verified against the live catalog ::: {#ed9b6ec7 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows where value_status != 'reported' but value is not NULL: 0 ``` ::: ::: Real counts by source, as of this render: ::: {#7f8bffb9 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
source value_status n
0 AHRF not_available 366
1 AHRF reported 64334
2 FARA not_available 73642
3 FARA reported 1380308
4 HPSA reported 2050
5 PLACES reported 3517402
6 PLACES suppressed_small_count 66
7 RUCA not_applicable 1384
8 RUCA reported 317676
9 RUCC not_available 2
10 RUCC reported 3233
11 SCP not_available 202230
12 SCP reported 1985478
13 SCP suppressed_small_count 14716116
14 SDWIS reported 16420
15 SVI not_available 7728
16 SVI reported 1190268
``` ::: ::: Two sources carry almost all of the suppression here. State Cancer Profiles' cancer counts are frequently small at the county level — its `suppressed_small_count` share dwarfs every other source's, exactly as expected for county-level cancer incidence and mortality. PLACES, model-based and published only above a minimum population threshold, has a much smaller suppressed slice. `not_available` on AHRF, FARA, RUCC and SVI is a blank source cell, not a suppression rule — the source simply didn't publish a value for that unit (see each source's page in [Sources](/sources.qmd) for its own missing-value convention). `not_applicable` on RUCA marks a zero-population, no-identifier tract — a real "this combination doesn't apply" case, not a hidden number. ## What this means for a query Never filter on `value IS NOT NULL` as a stand-in for "give me the real data" without also checking what's *behind* the NULLs you dropped — a county missing from your result because it's `suppressed_small_count` is a different finding than one missing because the source never covered it at all (`not_available`). The [suppressed-cells recipe](/recipes/suppressed-cells.qmd) runs this page's own query live, in your browser.
